components.name: Excise.Core project
components.targetState: Remain UI- and platform-independent; expose explicit, bounded domain APIs consumed by every delivery surface.

components.name: PDF primitives and object graph
components.targetState: Keep primitives deterministic, allocation-conscious, and free of workflow or UI policy.

components.name: Parser, xref, filters, and hostile-input boundary
components.targetState: Every attacker-controlled size, nesting level, loop, and resource allocation is bounded and fails with a typed diagnostic.

components.name: Encryption contracts, permissions, and standard security handler
components.targetState: One interoperable standard security handler owns password processing, permission contracts, encryption state, and cryptographic transforms below document and writer orchestration.

components.name: Document model and mutation boundary
components.targetState: Separate document lifetime, focused mutation services, and conservation policies so PdfDocument is not the accumulation point for unrelated workflows.

components.name: Content-stream walker and sinks
components.targetState: Keep one authoritative walk; new consumers add sinks or operator consumers and never duplicate PDF text/graphics state.

components.name: Font decoding, metrics, and subsetting
components.targetState: One font interpretation contract supplies extraction, geometry, redaction, authoring, and rendering without duplicated width/encoding tables.

components.name: Text extraction, ordering, search geometry, and selection
components.targetState: Share glyph decoding and geometry with redaction while keeping reading-order policy explicit and independently measured.

components.name: Glyph-, image-, and carrier-level redaction
components.targetState: Every shipping entry point uses the same fail-secure pipeline, and every security claim is judged by a non-Excise oracle or an explicit reason.

components.name: Fresh-write serialization and encryption preservation
components.targetState: All mutations conserve unrelated document properties unless a named policy deliberately removes them; outputs remain interoperable with independent readers.

components.name: Document conformance and structural validation
components.targetState: Document-dependent validation remains above the document and content engines, and every validation claim names its external oracle where one exists.

components.name: Excise.Rendering project
components.targetState: Keep rendering isolated behind a stable API; split implementation by responsibility while preserving a single explicit render context and oracle-backed behavior.

components.name: Excise.Ocr.Native project
components.targetState: Keep unsafe/native lifetime code isolated, source-generated where possible, and covered by platform-specific failure-path tests.

components.name: Excise.Ocr project
components.targetState: Remain an optional integration layer and stay off ordinary open/render paths until OCR is explicitly requested.

components.name: Excise.Avalonia project
components.targetState: Own viewer interaction/render scheduling without duplicating desktop-app workflow or PDF-domain policy.

components.name: Excise.Cli project
components.targetState: Program is composition and dispatch only; each command delegates to a focused handler sharing the same workflow services as other delivery surfaces.

components.name: Excise.App project
components.targetState: Keep composition and user-facing policy here while moving each primary workflow behind a focused controller/view-model with explicit state ownership.

components.name: Main-window orchestration and feature state
components.targetState: Become a thin workspace shell over separately testable document-session, navigation, redaction, editing, security, and background-workflow owners.

components.name: Repository verification system
components.targetState: Every gate is deterministic, mutation-proven, non-vacuous, and names whether it is a correctness proof, a ratchet, or an advisory measurement.

components.name: Architecture registry, reachability, and derived diagrams
components.targetState: Registry data, actual project references, source/evidence paths, current/target diagrams, and issue-linked gaps are checked together in t0.

relationships.rationale: Rendering consumes parsed operators but re-executes graphics/text state because rendering requires canvas, font, clipping, pattern, and Type3 hooks the glyph walker does not expose.
Glyph removal must use the one authoritative content walk and reconstruction path.
Content walking operates on the authoritative page and document object graph. PdfPage content compatibility members retain the public document API but are source-owned by the content engine.

Extraction, selection, and search geometry consume authoritative page, field, and coordinate contracts. PdfPage and PdfDocument text compatibility members retain the public document API but are source-owned by the text engine.
Text decoding and extraction interpret the parsed PDF object graph directly; redaction-owned references currently inflate this edge until #1321 establishes a distinct owner.
Document validation inspects tagging and operators through the authoritative content parser.
Temporary exception #1318: the content walker currently consumes text-owned glyph/CMap decoders and a nested TextExtractor sink; those shared contracts must move below the two engines.
Temporary exception #1319: content serialization consumes PdfNumberFormatter from writer ownership until the one canonical formatter moves to a neutral foundation.
The document model stores the active standard security handler and exposes established permission and re-encryption contracts without depending on document-level validation.
Temporary ownership exception #1320: font decoders consume AdobeGlyphList and StandardMacGlyphOrder from text ownership until the tables move under the font contract.

Temporary ownership exception #1321: ImageRegionRedactor is assigned to core-text because redaction has no non-overlapping owned source root; establish the redaction boundary and reclassify the dependency.
Independent saved-byte, extractor, and renderer checks must corroborate each security-relevant redaction assertion or record a specific exemption.
PDF-domain behavior must remain usable from CLI, desktop, tests, and other consumers without a UI dependency.
Architecture data and diagrams are part of the same fail-on-drift verification system as tests and API reachability.

workflows.name: Open, parse, render, navigate, search, and select

steps.responsibility: Resolve the input, own document lifetime, and surface user-visible failures.
Parse untrusted bytes with bounded recovery and typed diagnostics.
Expose pages, resources, annotations, and document state.
Rasterize the requested page and overlays.
Schedule visible pages, input, selection, accessibility, and viewport state.
Produce search, reading order, and selection geometry.

workflows.name: Select or name content, redact it, scrub carriers, and save a safe copy

steps.responsibility: Collect user intent and page/document coordinates without owning removal semantics.
Locate text using the shared glyph/reading model and expose confidence limits.
Remove glyphs/images and scrub positionless carriers under explicit policy.
Write a fresh output while preserving encryption policy and eliminating prior revisions.
Corroborate saved bytes, independent extraction, and rendered ink for the relevant property.

workflows.name: Edit pages, annotations, forms, or authored content and save

steps.responsibility: Own transient UI state and confirm destructive or permission-sensitive actions.
Apply typed mutations with conservation boundaries.
Serialize the modified object graph and encryption policy.
Preview and independently comparable reopened output.
Rasterize pages at the OCR contract resolution.
Own native engine lifetime and marshalling.
Interpret OCR results and construct text-layer operations.
Persist the searchable result.

workflows.name: Inspect signature structure, integrity, and trust

steps.responsibility: Parse the signed object graph and byte ranges without trusting declared lengths.
Validate byte ranges, CMS integrity, permissions, and structural status.
Evaluate platform trust where available and present integrity separately from trust.
Cross-check representative signatures and malformed ranges with independent tools/fixtures.

rules.statement: Excise.Core must not depend on Avalonia, SkiaSharp UI controls, delivery projects, or platform services.
New extraction, geometry, or redaction consumers use ContentStreamWalker semantics rather than implementing another PDF text-state parser.
A security-relevant redaction assertion uses a non-Excise oracle or carries a reviewed method-level reason.
Desktop, CLI, batch, and library entry points delegate to the same core mutation/security semantics rather than copy workflow policy.
Registry IDs, paths, project dependencies, workflow references, and current/target diagrams are validated and regenerated deterministically.
